title: DALL·E is a portmanteau of Salvador Dali, the Spanish surrealist, and WALL-E, Pixar's 2008 robot.
description:
DALL·E is a portmanteau of Salvador Dali, the Spanish surrealist, and WALL-E, Pixar's 2008 robot. OpenAI never spelled the joke out in dry technical language; the pun was already the headline when NBC News covered the launch.

OpenAI published DALL·E on 5 January 2021: a 12-billion-parameter version of GPT-3, retrained to generate images from text captions instead of continuing text. The model treats an image as 1,024 extra tokens tacked onto a caption's 256, then predicts all of them the way GPT-3 predicts words.

For every caption, DALL·E generated 512 candidate images, then used a second model called CLIP to rerank them down to the best 32. OpenAI stated none of its published examples were hand-picked beyond that automatic reranking.

parameters in the original DALL·E, a fraction of GPT-3's full size, repurposed entirely for pictures.

DALL·E turned out to be able to translate images the way GPT-3 translates text: performing image-to-image tasks it was never explicitly trained on. OpenAI's own paper says: "We did not anticipate that this capability would emerge, and made no modifications to the neural network or training procedure to encourage it."

Sources:
- https://openai.com/index/dall-e/: primary source; dated 5 January 2021, confirms DALL·E is a 12-billion-parameter version of GPT-3 retrained on text-image pairs, the token architecture (up to 256 text tokens plus 1,024 image tokens predicted autoregressively), the CLIP-reranking step that keeps the top 32 of 512 generated samples per caption, and the exact quote: "We did not anticipate that this capability would emerge, and made no modifications to the neural network or training procedure to encourage it."
- https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/innovation/here-s-dall-e-algorithm-learned-draw-anything-you-tell-n1255834: same-day (5 January 2021) coverage confirming the Salvador Dali/WALL-E naming pun was already the public framing of the launch, not a later retelling.
